arc: The teaching describes the cyclic mirror-wheel that stands before the Gate of the King of Honor — the mechanism by which every concealed motion of the bound archons in the firmaments is reflected outward and made known, so that the Lord's judicial truth governs the whole natural order without any falsity escaping its discrimination.
title: The Mirror-Wheel before the Gate of the King of Honor
reading:
This teaching unfolds a single image and presses it through to its judicial conclusion: there exists, set immediately before the Great Gate of the King of Honor, a turning Wheel which is at once a chain and a mirror — the cosmic prochos — and through it the entire bound order of the firmaments is held transparent to the ruling Divine Truth. The whole arc is one of vigilance: the Lord's discriminating presence at the threshold of the natural heavens does not merely contain the archons below and above, it reflects them, so that no movement of falsity can occur in secret.

The Wheel itself is the cyclic process of purification operating in ultimates — the turning of natural states under spiritual influence. What the teaching adds is that this turning carries a mirror-face. Set "before" (ⲍⲓⲧⲉⲍⲏ) the Gate of Honor, it is the receptive disc on which the inward state of every archon and every firmament is cast outward. The teaching tells us that the root of all the firmaments — those above and those below — together with the archons, is fashioned and stands fixed in this Wheel. Correspondentially, this is the truth that the entire ordered structure of the natural heavens has its origin held in the very mechanism of the Lord's judicial vigilance: the binding of the proprium and the ordering of natural truths share a single root, which is the discriminating presence of the King of Honor himself. The "great chain exceedingly" in which the archons are held is not separate from the Wheel; it is the same operation seen as restraint.

The interior of the Wheel is then opened. It is hidden in a gleam of the Radiance and adorned with twelve seals — the completeness in church / all aspects, the zodiacal articulation by which every quality of state is confirmed in correspondence. The middle seal, the central confirming imprint, is the five Men of Radiance who are joined together and fill the whole Zone. These are the five-fold descending Divine Truth — the complete natural-rational structure of the Lord's truth-attributes — set as the central girdle that holds every place, narrow or wide, transparent. Because the five-fold Living Soul of the Radiance fills the entire cosmic girdle, there is no place, however constricted or however broad, that is not present to the mirror.

From this construction the teaching draws its operative point. None of the bound archons wishes to release the bonds (none can will the dissolution of the chain that holds them); but if they wish to "work a deceit" in their fruit — that is, to bring forth some hidden falsity from their inner motion — the very wishing is manifested forth and known upon the prochos. The mirror's existence does not depend on their consent: it reveals. So too the spheres and the stars and all the powers of the zodiacal circuit — when they wish to release any motion, it is known and shown upon that prochos. The teaching draws the consequence in two complementary ways: as a chain before the Archphylax, the chief guardian, and as a great mirror for the judgment of all the works that are done in him. Chain and mirror are one operation: the bond holds, and the reflection exposes.

The spiritual process being taught is therefore the Lord's providential vigilance over the proprium and over every bound natural truth. Nothing rises in the firmaments — no thought of the archons, no movement of star or sphere, no narrow or hidden place of self-love — that does not stand already manifest before the discriminating Truth that rules at the Gate of Honor. The fear that "shall be borne by all the powers of the agreement" is the corresponding state in the bound: knowing themselves seen, no peering forth from the chain of their fruit is possible. This is the inner reason the natural heavens hold their order. Their order is not merely imposed from above as restraint; it is held by a reflective mechanism in which their own root stands. The Wheel is at once their origin (their root is fashioned in him), their bond (they stand in him as in a chain), and their judgment (their works are reflected upon him). 

Read as a whole, the teaching is a doctrine about how Divine Truth governs the mingled state without violence: by establishing in ultimates a turning mirror, sealed twelvefold and centered in the five descending attributes of the Radiance, against which every secret motion of falsity becomes its own self-disclosure. The Gate of Honor does not need to hunt the deceit; the deceit, in the very wishing, paints itself upon the prochos and is judged.
